text.content:
The Forward-Planting Script

GM-only. Every line below is something to say at the table during Phase 2 so that a later phase has something to land on. They are ordered by the phase they pay off in. Each entry gives you the plant, the moment to use it, the line itself, and the hard limit on how far you may go.

The rule that governs all of them: a seed is a shape, not an explanation. If the party asks a follow-up question, the honest answer is almost always "no one here can tell you that." Resist improving your own seeds.

Pays off in Phase 3 — Hardby

Plant: the living hand is in Hardby. Use it when the bearer instrument comes out of the lozenge tin, or when Hesren Vesh's guard drops for one sentence.

Caelith, very evenly: "That is a Hardby chop. That is the Hardby chop. The man who put it on this paper put it on Vandrell's escrow. We do not have a face yet. We have the hand."

Limit: no name for the hand. Solen Mereth is Veska's reveal in Phase 3, not yours in Phase 2.

Plant: a person is on a clock. Any time the party dawdles — Trina, in passing, never pressing: "Ailen Moraven is nineteen and she is in Hardby, and nobody has told her anything."

Pays off in Phase 4 — Rel Astra

Plant: the phrase is a calendar, not a motto. When the vellum strip is read, let Caelith turn it over and decline to solve it:

"Harbor before throne. That is not a threat and it is not a prayer. That is a sequence. Somebody is doing things in an order, and the order matters more to them than the doing."

Plant: the partner who signs nothing. Only if the party pushes Vesh on who could authorise the endorsement. Vesh, stiffly, quoting his own training: "Marginal endorsements are the privilege of a senior partner. We have two. One of them has not signed a letter at his own desk in eleven years, and I am told he is unwell." Limit: Vesh does not know the name. He has never been told it.

Pays off in Phase 5 — the leak, and the woman in the wood

Plant: the seal that shouldn't exist. When Sarth's forged writ is recovered, do not let Caelith be neutral about it. He goes quiet, then: "I have been looking for that stamp for nine months. It is made in my own building." Then he refuses to say more: "I will not name a clerk I cannot prove."

Plant: the recruitment pattern. Twice in Phase 2, the phrase the man on the lane should be in the air — Reith describing the "watch-coat man," Sparrow describing who leaves her coppers. Phase 5's Ostren Pell uses the same words for his handler, and Sera's shop is on the same Wick Lane. Never point at it. Let it rhyme.

Plant (repair — see Seed Repairs): Trina's correspondent in the wood. Phase 4's Letter 4 refers to "my old correspondent in the wood" as though the party should recognise it. Currently they never hear of her in Phase 2. Fix it here, in Trina's mouth, in the Records Alcove:

"I know a woman who could tell you more from the wax than you will get from the writing. She lives west, past the good roads, and she does not answer letters from people she has not met. I have not asked her for anything in six years. I would rather not spend that on a coin."

Limit: no name, no location, no species. She is a favour Trina is not ready to spend.

Pays off in Phase 6 — Greyhawk

Plant: Greyhawk is where frightened people go. Pollow asks for two days and names the destination himself — "I have a cousin in Greyhawk" — and if he dies instead, the one line he leaves is "the man at the Brass Crow." Either way the city gets named by someone who is afraid.

Plant: paper moves on a schedule, eastward. The Sparrow fold's routing line — "east on the Sevenday cart" — plus the drop behind the Coopers' Arms. What the party should absorb is not the destination but the shape: somebody runs a letter agency, and letter agencies have far ends.

Plant (repair): the courier's side-mark. A small vertical stroke crossed at three-quarter height, in the corner of the Sparrow fold's instruction card and on the wax flap of Vesh's outgoing courier packet. Describe it exactly once, in passing, as "a little crossed stroke in the corner, the sort of mark a house uses to sort its own post." Never explain it. In Phase 6 it is beside H. V. Andren in the Brass Crow registry; in Phase 8 it is on every registry fragment below Tarnsmere. This is the campaign's longest single payoff and it costs you one sentence now.

Pays off in Phases 7–9 — the descent

Plant: the tube is the only downward hint in the chapter. Every reading stops at "elven, but peculiar." Legend lore returns a fragmentary verse about a people who walked downward and were forgotten, and the caster cannot place it. Limit, absolute: no Drow, no Underdark, no Eilserv, no Erelhei-Cinlu, not under any roll, not as a hint, not as a "you feel that…"

Plant (repair): the negative space in the map tube. When the routes are laid out, count them out loud — sea, trade, caravan — and let Caelith close the circle: "Three ways to move a thing between two cities, and that is all the ways there are." In Phase 6 the party reads No sail. No road. and the floor goes out from under that sentence. You do not need them to remember it consciously; you need it to have been said.

Plant: people carried as accounts. The ledger fragment's three verbs are the campaign's thesis. Say them slowly — settled, delayed, transferred — and let Caelith name the wrongness without solving it: "Real settlement work carries figures. This carries names." In Phase 9 the party reads "H.V.A. — Recovered cargo" on a stone counter and this sentence detonates six phases late.

Pays off much later — do not touch

The Hardby barmaid of 580. Named once in Caelith's speech as a loose end he never identified. If asked, his answer is exact and final: "She was, when I went looking, also not there." Canon is in the GM-only page of the Start Here journal; leave it there.

Per-PC Narration Beats — Phase 2

GM-only. The per-PC threads live in full in the Per-PC Plot Threads journal; this page tells you which beat fires in this chapter, in which scene, and what to say. One beat per player per session is the correct dose. If a player is not engaging with their thread, skip theirs without ceremony.

The delivery rule: these are given to the player, quietly, in a sentence or two — not announced to the table, not rolled for, never explained afterward. A beat that gets discussed stops being a beat.

Alicia Trévanne — The Pact Silence

Fires in: Movement One (the burned focus and the wax), and any Trina scene.

The beat: when she handles the melted wax on the focus, her pact-mark goes cold. Not painful. Cold the way a room is cold when a door has been opened somewhere else in the house.

"Your mark has been quiet for a while now — attentive, but quiet. When your thumb crosses that wax it goes cold, and stays cold for as long as you are touching it."

Trina's half, privately, if they are alone: "Yours is silent too?" — and then she changes the subject, permanently. Limit: Trina never names her patron in this chapter. Insight past the wall returns only "I share a teacher with you. I have not finished my lessons."

Kitty Raleigh — Chthonic Recognition

Fires in: Movement One (the E. sigil) and — the strong one — the Grain Register, if you use the blight-specimen beat.

The beat, at the wax: her sigil-veining warms faintly for a few seconds when she touches the E. seal. Not magic she can use. Recognition without vocabulary — the way you know a relative's handwriting before you know the name.

The beat, at the blight: unstopper a Grain Register specimen jar near her. The tendrils lean before she decides anything. The blighted grain is years dead and it is the most alive thing her body has noticed since the Keep, and underneath the warmth is a wordless certainty: this was made, and what made it is old, and it is far below her. Then hand her the proof of concept: the sterile show-grain from the seed pouch gives her nothing at all. Cold as gravel. Her tendrils have just become the party's forgery detector.

Limit: tuned to residue of the working — blight, E.-wax, and much later the deep marks. Never to people, never to allegiance, or the mystery structure collapses.

Gianni Varren — Geographic Erasure

Fires in: the map tube, and any street work on the way to Tannerway.

The beat: she knows these roads. Laying the caravan chart flat, she notices an eastern trade-spur she walked as a girl is simply not on it — and the omission is clean, not sloppy: the cartographer drew around the gap.

"You have walked that spur. You have slept on it. It is not that the map is old — the map is current, and the spur is gone from it the way a name is gone from a page somebody re-copied on purpose."

Limit: one spur, not four. The full pattern is her Phase 4 payoff at the imperial survey.

Selvara Stormborn — Dreams of Cut Stone

Fires in: any night the party sleeps in the Little Palace after the daylight review.

The beat: the descending stair again, torchlight, a procession she is part of. This time she gets as far as the seventh step, and there is a mark cut into the wall at her shoulder that she cannot focus on. She wakes with the number seven and no reason for it.

"You wake at the seventh step. You always wake at the seventh step. The mark was at your shoulder and you could not make your eyes hold it."

Limit: she never counts the cuts, and no divination clarifies the mark. It clarifies for the first time when she is standing in front of the cairn.

Ellyndra "Elle" Swiftfoot — The Sealed Records of Her Order

Fires in: devotions at the Loftwick temple — give her one, unprompted, the morning after the gaol.

The beat: the hymnal on the shelf has an older hand in the margin beside a prayer she has never been taught: "Pray for those who descended. May the second bell ring for them above." The resident priest shrugs at it — an old house custom, he thinks; ask the Cloister.

Second, harder beat (the gaol): her network is her thread's engine, and Thimblecut is her acquaintance. Let her feel the specific weight of it — someone reached a person who trusted her, in a room built so nothing can reach anyone.

Limit: nobody explains the second bell in this chapter. It opens the box in Phase 5 and unscrews into a descent token in Phase 8. If she chases it now, the Cloister's answer is "Brother Ashan keeps the older records, and he is at Hardby chapter until the spring."

Cam — The Halfling Networks (dormant)

Status: her player is assumed out. Keep the thread intact, unspoken, and ready to hand back whole.

If she returns: her Phase 2 beat is a folded note from a network contact — "Three farms gone quiet east of Pleasant Hill. Not bandits. Not weather. Asking around." — and it connects to nothing yet, which is the point.

If she does not: the payoff transfers to Elle, who inherits Hesp Olfair's list of thirty-one eastbound halflings who did not come back, and reads the "Return: nil" cousins on the Tarnsmere registry in Phase 8. Do not re-cast the beat for anyone else; Elle's own thread absorbs it cleanly.

Any PC with no live thread

Give them the room instead of the omen: the one who notices the scribe's hand shaking, the one the frightened landlord decides to talk to, the one Trina asks a real question. Threads are a spice. Attention is the meal.

pages.name: Seed Repairs — What Phase 2 Was Missing

text.content:
Seed Repairs — What Phase 2 Was Missing

GM-only. An audit of this chapter against Phases 5–9 turned up four things later chapters expect the party to have met, which Phase 2 as written never gives them. Each repair below is small, costs no scene time, and is written ready to say. Use all four; they are the cheapest structural work in the campaign.

Repair 1 — Trina's correspondent in the wood (pays off in Phase 5)

The gap: Caelith's Phase 4 Letter 4 mentions that Trina has sent a copy of the Hardby opinion to "my old correspondent in the wood," and Phase 5 opens a sealed packet from that woman as if the party has been waiting for it. As written, they have never heard of her.

Where: the Records Alcove, while Trina is being useful with the Marks Volume. What to say:

"There is a woman who could tell you more from the wax than from the writing — she reads matter, the way a notary reads a hand. She lives west, past the good roads. She does not answer letters from people she has not met, and I have not asked her for anything in six years." A pause. "I would rather not spend that on a coin."

Limit: no name, no distance, no species, no favour granted. If the party presses, Trina simply declines. The whole job of the repair is that in Phase 5, when Caelith says "Trina's correspondent in the wood has answered," a player says "oh — her."

Repair 2 — the courier's side-mark (pays off in Phases 6 and 8)

The gap: Kethren's foreign-correspondent mark — a vertical stroke crossed at three-quarter height — is the single object that ties the Greyhawk registry to the under-road registries a hundred miles and two chapters later. Phase 6 treats it as a recognition. Phase 2 currently gives them nothing to recognise.

Where, twice: in the corner of the Sparrow fold's instruction card; and on the wax flap of the sealed packet Hesren Vesh's courier carries out of Wick Lane, if a PC gets eyes on it.

"In the corner, small: a single upright stroke with a short bar across it, up near the top. The sort of mark a house puts on its own post so the right desk gets it."

Limit: it means nothing, resolves to nothing, and no check improves it. If a player sketches it in their notes, you have already won.

Repair 3 — Elle's second-bell prayer (pays off in Phases 5 and 8)

The gap: Elle's iron key is the campaign's seventh way through the Permission Door, and her order's 374 CY expedition is the reason it exists. Phase 5 opens that box. Nothing in Phases 2 or 3 tells her there is a box.

Where: a temple morning, unprompted, the day after the gaol. What: a marginal line in an old hymnal — "Pray for those who descended. May the second bell ring for them above." The resident priest has wondered about it for years and assumes it is a house custom.

Limit: the Cloister's keeper of the older records is away until spring. She cannot open this in Phase 2, and should not.

Repair 4 — the three surface roads (pays off in Phase 6)

The gap: No sail. No road. lands in Phase 6 as a phrase that ought to be impossible. It only feels impossible if somebody once said out loud that there are three ways to move a thing and that is all of them.

Where: the map tube, Movement One, as the charts come out. What to say:

Caelith, counting them off: "Sea. Trade road. Caravan track. Three ways to move a thing between two cities, and that is all the ways there are."

Limit: do not draw attention to it, do not repeat it, and never let anyone in Phase 2 or 3 propose a fourth.

Optional fifth — the table's own thread (Sara Thimblecut)

Not a module seed; your table made this one. Thimblecut was poisoned mid-name in the gaol. Recommended canon: the name under her finger was Gilst, and what she was about to say is that she saw him carried out of the Shambord House by night after his recorded death. Whether she lives is yours; the fact re-derives at the Shambord House either way, from a neighbour who heard the night-move. If you take this, the poisoning becomes the first hard evidence that the watcher apparatus on Wick Lane can reach inside a Yeomanry gaol — which is exactly the sentence Phase 5's leak operation wants the party carrying.

pages.name: Beat Map — Which Scene Fires What

text.content:
Beat Map — Which Scene Fires What

GM-only. A one-screen index of this chapter: for each scene, the plants and per-PC beats that belong to it. Run down this list while you prep and mark the two or three you intend to use tonight. Nothing here is mandatory except the items in the Five Truths.

Movement One — The Table

Scene 1 · The Morning Review. Plants: none required. Beat: Alicia — the pact-mark goes cold at the wax.

Scene 1 · Caelith's Hand-of-the-Duke Speech. Plants: the office is not secure (→ Phase 5); the Hardby barmaid of 580 (deep future, never resolved).

Scene 1 · The Seven Items. Plants: settled / delayed / transferred spoken slowly (→ Phase 9); "elven, but peculiar" and the legend-lore verse (→ Phases 7–9); "three ways to move a thing" (Repair 4, → Phase 6); "harbor before throne is a sequence" (→ Phase 4). Beats: Kitty — veining warms at the E. sigil; Gianni — the missing trade-spur on the caravan chart.

Scene 2 · Records Alcove. Plants: Cindren & Vhal named; the Wick Lane satellite; Repair 1 — Trina's correspondent in the wood.

Movement Two — The City

Scene 3a · The Firm's Door (Hesren Vesh). Plants: "reads like Hardby work" (→ Phase 3); the senior partner who has not signed at his own desk in eleven years (→ Phase 4); Repair 2 — the side-mark on his courier's wax flap.

Scene 3b · The Dead Man's Rooms. Plants: the Hardby chop on the bearer instrument — "we have the hand" (→ Phase 3); the three "E." countersigns (→ the whole campaign); the fear note read aloud. Beat: Elle — if she is the one Reith decides to trust, let that be visible.

Scene 3c · Reln Pollow. Plants: Greyhawk named by a frightened man; if he dies, "the man at the Brass Crow" (→ Phase 6).

Scene 3d · The Sparrow's Run. Plants: "east on the Sevenday cart" and the city drop (→ Phases 5–6); Repair 2 — the side-mark in the fold's corner. Beat: whoever corners her — the moral test; Trina will take her in without being asked.

Scene 4a · The Counting House (Doril Veth). Plants: claims filed before their losses (→ Phases 3 and 9); the stolen carbons — someone was here first. Beat: Kitty — the blight specimens, if you route the Grain Register jars through this visit.

Scene 4b · Vellin Moraven. Plants: Ailen is in Hardby (→ Phase 3, and the stall-breaker for the whole chapter).

Scene 4c · Sergeant Anwic. Plants: the Watch is honest and outmatched — institutions used, not bought (→ Phase 5).

Interlude · The Mentor. Beat: Alicia — Trina's "Yours is silent too?"

Movement Three — The Squeeze and the Road

Scene 5 · Arthen Moll. Plants: the polite face of containment; Moll is sincere, which is worse (→ Phase 5's Brane).

Scene 6 · Merev Sarth. Plants: "Tarsh" (→ Phase 3); the forged Audit Hall seal and Caelith's refusal to name a clerk (→ Phase 5).

Scene 7 · Three Roads East. Plants: the road choice itself; Trina's letter to Castrian Vell (→ Phase 3). Run the Five Truths gate check before the folios hit the table.

Ending · Departing East. Plants: the brass Hand-token and the folded paper for the Mossen Place (→ Phase 3, read on the road).

Sidequest — The Sign of the Brown Hare

Plants: the "R." is a person, not a door (the chapter's one honest red herring); the cedar box and the never-sent letter (→ Phase 6, where Rosalin's name returns). Beat: any PC with a sibling, living or otherwise — this is the scene for it.

Coverage check

By the end of the chapter every player should have had at least one beat from this page spoken to them directly. If you can name a player who has not, give them theirs during the ride south or the night before departure — both are quiet enough to carry it.
